title: New evidence for rice harvesting in the early Neolithic Lower Yangtze River, China
version: PLOS ONE, 17(12), e0278200; version of record.
lineage: Original use-wear and phytolith residue analyses on excavated flakes, distinct from the Shangshan sediment phytolith samples used to infer domestication traits.

passages.locator: Integrating use-wear and phytolith results, Figs. 6–8
passages.note: Specimen SS-10 from Shangshan combines predominantly transverse striations with rice-husk phytoliths, interpreted as cutting panicles. Botanical residues and use-wear provide different proxies on the same flakes.

The authors propose that repeated selective panicle harvest can bias seed stocks towards non-shattering rice if later harvests are kept for sowing. SS-10 directly informs the technique but does not test seed selection for a particular population or the silica traits studied by Zuo and colleagues.
